summary: Added a versioned AOT cache envelope that validates format, schema version, exact argument-derived cache key, filename binding, and CompiledArtifact payload type. Malformed, corrupt, or incompatible artifacts now raise an explicit RuntimeError instead of becoming a cache miss and silently falling back to JIT compilation. Existing runtime-scalar cache-key behavior remains covered.

tests.what_was_measured: Five schema validation/round-trip regressions and four existing scalar/cache-key regressions; 9 passed.
Related cache-key completeness, target/hint identity, and AOT schema behavior; 35 passed and 2 architecture-dependent tests skipped.

tests.command: FLYDSL_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR=/job/aot-schema-work/cache FLYDSL_RUNTIME_ENABLE_CACHE=1 python /job/aot-schema-work/aot_vecadd_fresh_process.py; FLYDSL_RUNTIME_RUN_ONLY=1 with the same command in a second process
tests.what_was_measured: A real gfx950/MI350X vector-add artifact was exported and loaded in a fresh run-only process. Both processes produced max_error=0 and checksum=39.3016815 versus the independent PyTorch a+b reference. The serialized compiled MLIR is 13061 bytes and contains gpu.binary, rocdl.target, amdgpu, and gfx950 evidence.
An incompatible constexpr argument schema failed with an explicit no-usable-AOT-cache RuntimeError and did not compile.
A schema_version=999 artifact failed during cache loading with an Invalid FlyDSL AOT cache artifact RuntimeError even though normal JIT was enabled, demonstrating no silent fallback.

gpu_execution_evidence: Two distinct processes (PIDs 2881 and 2973) executed on AMD Instinct MI350X; the second used run-only loading and matched PyTorch exactly. Raw logs: /job/aot-schema-work/raw/gpu_export_process.txt and /job/aot-schema-work/raw/gpu_load_fresh_process.txt.
remaining_limitations: This is a Python cache-format change and does not require rebuilding FlyDSL's native library. Pre-schema raw-pickle cache files are deliberately rejected with a clear incompatibility error and must be regenerated. The envelope validates compatibility/integrity metadata after deserialization; it does not make pickle safe for artifacts supplied by an untrusted party.
